title: Neuro-Fuzzy Concept Learning for Interpretable Large Multimodal Models
claim: A frozen multimodal model's token representations are fuzzified, defuzzified into interpretable concepts, then grounded in text and images.
layout: 3 dashed panels, left-to-right, LMM diagram feeding fuzzy loop, grounding on right
description: The figure is a three-part pipeline inside dashed rounded boxes. On the left, a blue frozen LMM block shows an Unembed layer, stacked FFN/SA blocks, and rows of green token embeddings. A mapping module and perceptual encoder sit below, with a bus photo as input. One orange token, highlighted in red, is pulled out through an arrow. In the middle, the 'Hybrid Neuro-Fuzzy Concept Extraction' panel runs as a loop. The representation matrix Z (blue grid with a bus icon) goes to a green Fuzzification box (Gaussian membership, normalized firing strengths, TSK polynomials). It then yields purple fuzzy activations V and a green Defuzzification equation box, and ends in an orange neuro-fuzzy concepts matrix U. On the right, a Multimodal Concept Grounding panel maps U_j through an Embed (W_U) step to top text tokens, and maps V_j through a Find Most Activating Samples step to bus photos. The eye goes first to the large blue LMM block and then to the green fuzzy boxes.

abstract: Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) integrate unimodal encoders with Large Language Models (LLMs) to execute complex multimodal tasks. Despite progress in the field, understanding the internal representations of these models through interpretable logic remains an open problem. To address this, we present a framework utilizing a Human-Inspired (Neuro-fuzzy) approach for learning token representations. In this method, we leverage fuzzy rules to compute activation firing strengths, which are subsequently defuzzified to extract distinct concepts. This mechanism allows for the interpretation of learned representations directly through explicit logic. Consequently, we derive "multimodal concepts" that are both semantically coherent and interpretable. We validate our approach through rigorous qualitative and quantitative experiments, demonstrating the utility of these concepts in interpreting test samples. Additionally, we evaluate the disentanglement of the learned concepts and the efficacy of their grounding in both visual and textual domains.
